claims: Gasoline is a transparent, flammable liquid refined from petroleum.
Gasoline contains a mixture of hydrocarbons and additives.
Gasoline is primarily used as fuel for spark-ignited internal combustion engines in vehicles.
Gasoline is produced by fractional distillation in refineries.
Regular, mid-grade, premium.
Gasoline is a complex mixture of roughly 150 organic compounds.
Gasoline's organic compounds are primarily hydrocarbons like benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX).
Gasoline includes detergents.
Gasoline includes anti-icing agents.
Gasoline includes anti-rust agents.
Gasoline includes anti-knock agents.
Most US gasoline is blended with about 10% fuel ethanol by volume.
Gasoline is produced in petroleum refineries through the distillation of crude oil.
Gasoline components are blended to meet specific performance standards such as octane ratings.
Gasoline primarily powers cars, SUVs, motorcycles, light trucks, and small aircraft.
Gasoline powers small engines such as lawnmowers, chain saws, and generators.
Regular gasoline has 87 octane.
Regular gasoline is the most common grade.
Mid-grade gasoline has 89 octane.
Mid-grade gasoline is an intermediate option.
Premium gasoline has 91-94 octane.
Premium gasoline is used for higher-performance engines to prevent knocking.
Burning gasoline releases greenhouse gases such as CO2.
As of March 2026, geopolitical events have created gasoline price instability.
